back: Where a firm or industry sets up production, chosen to keep costs low and reach markets and inputs.
Raw materials, markets, labour, power, transport, water, land, external economies, government policy.
Inputs heavier or bulkier than output (sugar milling, smelting): locates near raw materials.
Output heavier, bulkier or more fragile than inputs (brewing, soft drinks): locates near the market.
A selected rural centre where government concentrates infrastructure and services to attract firms and spread development.
Reduce regional inequality, rural-urban migration and urban congestion; develop resources in remote areas.
Incentives (tax holidays, grants, cheap sites), infrastructure, growth points, restrictions (zoning), siting public-sector activities.
Remote areas may still have small markets and few skills, so firms face higher costs and may leave when incentives end.
